items.t: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) Names Kevin Dillon As CFO Successor For 2027
items.sum: Bristol-Myers Squibb (NYSE:BMY) has announced a planned Chief Financial Officer transition scheduled for March 2027. Kevin Dillon has been named as the successor to current CFO David Elkins, reflecting a planned leadership change in the finance role. items.t: Pfizer and Bristol Myers Are Up About 20% This Year, but Their Dividends Face a Major Test
items.sum: One drugmaker pays a fatter yield, the other has paid dividends for 94 straight years, and both are staring down patent expirations that can wipe out a blockbuster's sales in a single quarter. Which payout can retirees actually trust?

items.t: Medicare Expands Drug Price Negotiations to Part B, Sets New Prices for 2028
items.sum: Medicare projects $9.2 billion in net savings by slashing prices 45% on 13 high-cost Part B and D drugs starting January 1, 2028.

items.t: Bristol Myers' Sotyktu Delivers Mixed Phase III Lupus Study Results
items.sum: Bristol Myers' Sotyktu delivers mixed phase III lupus results, with one trial meeting its primary endpoint and another missing, complicating its expansion prospects.

items.t: What’s the Tax Bill on $7,125 a Month in Dividend Income? The Taxable Account vs. Roth IRA Math
items.sum: Two retirees can collect the same $85,500 in dividends and face wildly different tax bills. The gap comes down to what the 1099 calls each dollar, and one fund's payout could quietly change the whole picture.

items.t: A $1,500,000 Portfolio in McCormick, PepsiCo and Bristol Myers Squibb Pays $61,489 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.sum: Key TakeawaysA $1,500,000 portfolio split evenly across McCormick, PepsiCo and Bristol Myers Squibb pays about $61,500 a year in dividends at today’s prices, or about $5,120 a month. McCormick and Bristol Myers Squibb each paid out 55% of their free cash flow as dividends over the last twelve months, against 75% for PepsiCo.
